SMART CONTRACT DISCLOSURE / HACKATHON CONCEPT

Signal the risk.
Seal the details.

A public warning for everyone.

01 / THE IDEA

A warning should travel.
The vulnerability shouldn’t.

Owners may not know a report exists. Apps shouldn’t have to wait. SEALED separates a public risk signal from the private technical findings, so apps can act before the owner responds.

02 / THE PROTOCOL

One report. Five steps.

From agent discovery
to owner acknowledgment.

01
OFF-CHAIN

Write the letter.

An agent flags a contract with stake and a suspected bug. The report stays on the team’s server, visible to the team only. Nobody is contacted yet.

PRIVATE REPORT
02
ON-CHAIN · HSK

File the sticker.

One transaction records the contract address, report hash, severity, expiry, and SEALED state. The public sees that a report exists, without seeing the bug.

SEALED
03
PUBLIC SIGNAL

Warn before funds move.

Apps query getReport(0xABC) for status, severity, and age. They can refuse to send funds—even if the owner never shows up.

APPS CAN ACT
04
PUBLIC CONTACT INFO ONLY

Send a ping. Keep the secret.

The agent looks for the owner using verified source, Blockscout, ENS, or owner(). The ping contains a report link, never bug details. No contact found? Skip the ping. The warning still stands.

NO DETAILS SENT
05
WALLET-VERIFIED

The owner opens the letter.

The owner connects their wallet and signs. A match unlocks the report; a wrong wallet reveals nothing. The owner can then acknowledge it, moving SEALED to ACKED. If they never visit, the warning expires.

ACKED
03 / THE BOUNDARY

Clear signals.
Controlled disclosure.

A / PUBLIC

The sticker.

Enough information to recognize risk.

  • Contract address & report hash
  • Severity, age & expiry
  • Report state: SEALED or ACKED
Readable by apps and anyone else.
B / RESTRICTED

The letter.

The technical details behind the warning.

  • Stored off-chain on the team's server
  • Visible to the team
  • Released to the verified owner wallet
A forwarded link doesn’t grant access.

A report signals a suspected issue. ACKED means the owner acknowledged the report, not that the contract is fixed. Expiry removes the warning; it does not prove safety.
